title: Basin-scale underwater positioning without surfacing

concept.text: The innovation would be a persistent positioning service that lets a moving underwater vehicle determine its location across an ocean basin while remaining submerged. Its proposed acoustic form uses a small number of distant sound sources as reference points: the vehicle measures acoustic ranges and uses them to estimate its position. DARPA’s Positioning System for Deep Ocean Navigation (POSYDON) summary documents this basin-scale goal, including continuous, accurate positioning without surfacing for GPS.

Proposed scope: the service would maintain useful positioning accuracy over multi-week to multi-month mobile missions using sparse, remote sources, without installing a transponder field around each operating area. This extends the documented program goal into an operational target. A propagation model, an isolated acoustic fix or a stationary seafloor measurement would each address part of the problem, but would not establish this persistent mobile capability.

significance.text: Conventional GPS reception is unavailable beneath seawater, according to DARPA’s POSYDON summary. Dependable basin-scale submerged positioning would therefore remove a major navigation constraint: vehicles could obtain position updates during long underwater missions without surfacing for satellite fixes. A service using common acoustic references could also give multiple submerged vehicles a shared geographic frame.

Conditional impact assessment: reliable coverage with bounded errors for months could substantially extend underwater autonomy, support repeatable survey routes and help vehicles return to mapped work sites. Coordinated fleets and sustained work without a nearby tender would become more plausible, but would still depend on communications, control, energy, reliability and mission support. Position information alone would not deliver those outcomes.

The comparison with GPS expresses the potential reach and usefulness of a common positioning service throughout a large operating volume. It does not establish GPS-like accuracy, availability, update rate, cost or adoption. Nor would acoustic positioning itself supply high-rate underwater communications or reveal other objects throughout the ocean: those remain distinct capabilities represented by MNE-06 and MNE-10.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central capability to establish is reliable conversion of long-range acoustic measurements into an accurate position for a moving receiver across a basin. DARPA’s division of POSYDON into propagation-channel modeling, waveform development and a system demonstration identifies essential parts of that task. A usable service would have to combine these parts into sustained positioning performance rather than demonstrate each only in isolation.

Engineering considerations retained from the research, with an evidence qualification: the proposed system must account for sound-speed changes associated with temperature, salinity and pressure, as well as internal-wave effects and multiple acoustic paths that can complicate travel-time interpretation. These mechanisms explain why a measured arrival time may not translate simply into geometric distance. The supplied review establishes the relevance of propagation modeling, but its source material does not substantiate these mechanisms individually or quantify their effects on the proposed service.

Proposed engineering requirements also include usable source geometry, reliable identification of acoustic arrivals, sufficiently known source positions, timing stability, receiver motion estimation and an honest estimate of positioning uncertainty during poor reception. The earlier claim that the fluctuating channel is the fundamental barrier rather than clocks is too strong for the available evidence. Channel uncertainty, timing and other system errors need a measured error budget before their relative importance can be ranked.

The sparse-source and long-duration requirements make coverage a system problem as well as a ranging problem. A convincing solution would need to show where position estimates remain available, how errors evolve between useful measurements and how the vehicle recognizes degraded service. These are proposed practical requirements; the supplied evidence does not establish whether an existing system already satisfies them.

current_state.text: The supplied review reports that DARPA’s POSYDON page marks the program complete and the page no longer maintained. Its retained summary describes Phase I as propagation-channel modeling, Phase II as waveform development and Phase III as a scheduled full system demonstration. The reviewed page gives no achieved positioning accuracy and reports no deployed basin-scale service. A program-completion notice does not by itself establish technical success, failure or deployment, and the absence of performance results on this page is not evidence that no demonstration occurred.

WHOI’s Slocum glider overview provides operational context for long-duration underwater vehicles: the reviewed text describes weeks-to-months endurance, GPS equipment and waypoint updates through Iridium communication sessions. It does not explicitly state that the vehicles surface to use those functions. It therefore supports the endurance and equipment description, but not the earlier attribution of an explicit surfacing statement or a general conclusion about how all long-duration underwater vehicles navigate.

The evidence has a limited temporal and technical scope. Both supplied pages are undated and were retrieved on November 11, 2026; those retrieval dates do not establish their contents on the review’s November 1, 2026 assessment date. The supplied freshness-search record is empty. Although the source index reports no extraction errors or truncation, the review treats the DARPA landing page as partial technical evidence because it contains a program summary rather than a performance evaluation; it treats the retained WHOI overview as complete for that page. These materials establish the documented ambition and the glider context, but cannot establish the field-wide availability or absence of this capability at either date.

The earlier comparisons with regional acoustic baselines and terrain matching remain unverified within this evidence set. They can frame future comparisons involving infrastructure and map dependence, but cannot serve here as an established inventory of available alternatives. No achieved months-long positioning accuracy, basin-wide availability figure or quantitative comparison with those alternatives is established by the supplied review.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: a mobile test vehicle remains submerged while traversing a deep-ocean basin for at least several weeks and obtains continuous positioning from a sparse, pre-existing set of remote acoustic sources rather than a locally installed array. Require errors to remain within a few tens of metres over the trial. The duration, accuracy and infrastructure conditions are proposed acceptance criteria, not established standards or documented DARPA specifications. They operationalize the basin-scale submerged-positioning ambition described by POSYDON.
completion_criteria.label: Weeks-long submerged basin positioning stays within a few tens of metres

completion_criteria.text: Proposed verification: compare the service’s estimates with an independent reference trajectory of adequate accuracy and temporal coverage throughout the mission. A position check only at the end cannot establish that errors stayed bounded along the route. The trial should define its update interval, tolerated outages and treatment of missing fixes in advance, then report error distributions, worst observed errors, availability and uncertainty estimates. The reference system’s own uncertainty and any shared error sources must be disclosed.
completion_criteria.label: Mission-wide reference comparisons establish positioning errors, availability and uncertainty

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirements: repeat trials across materially different routes, depths and ocean conditions, including conditions expected to challenge reception and propagation modeling. Release enough information about source locations and timing, waveform processing, environmental assumptions, receiver motion and reference measurements for independent assessment, with independent replication where feasible. Several-week trials would establish performance over that duration; claims of multi-month operation would require corresponding evidence. Finite trials establish demonstrated breadth, not literal coverage of every location and condition.
completion_criteria.label: Repeated trials demonstrate performance across differing routes and ocean conditions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: report the geographic and depth envelope, source spacing, installation and maintenance requirements, receiver power and size, and any dependence on external environmental updates or supporting communications. A channel model or a stationary benchmark positioned from a surface ship would remain a partial contribution. Completion at the proposed scope requires mobile, sustained, submerged positioning with measured accuracy and availability across the claimed operating envelope.
completion_criteria.label: Operating envelope, infrastructure dependencies and receiver requirements are reported

related_concepts.text: MNE-06, Through-seawater links beyond the acoustic range–rate ceiling, overlaps through the underwater propagation environment and potentially shared signaling infrastructure. Its objective is communication performance; MNE-05 concerns obtaining position. Successful positioning would not establish a high-rate data link, and a capable link would not by itself establish accurate navigation.

MNE-10, Coherent observability of the deep-ocean volume, concerns observing the surrounding ocean volume and objects within it. MNE-05 concerns a receiver determining its own location relative to known references. Positioning could help place observations in a common geographic frame, but locating a cooperative receiver would not demonstrate long-range detection or tracking of other objects.

MNE-07, Persistent abyssal work, with depth no longer the cost driver, and MNE-08, Work-class underwater vehicles powered by the ocean, could benefit from dependable submerged navigation. MNE-07 addresses the practicality and cost of sustained deep work; MNE-08 addresses vehicle energy supply. Positioning could support repeatable routes and returns to work sites, while neither affordable depth access nor ocean-derived power alone supplies a common position reference.

MNE-01, Ship-scale collapse of turbulent skin friction; MNE-02, Merchant ships freed from the displacement-hull speed barrier; MNE-03, Seawater magnetohydrodynamic propulsion at propeller-class efficiency; and MNE-04, Controlled, sustained supercavitating travel, address distinct drag, speed or propulsion advances. Their overlap with MNE-05 is operational: a moving platform may need navigation. Achieving any of those motion capabilities would not establish basin-scale underwater positioning, and positioning would not resolve their respective physical barriers.

MNE-09, Storm-stable floating land in the open ocean, concerns the stability and habitability of a surface structure. Such a platform might hypothetically host positioning infrastructure, but that is an architectural possibility rather than a dependency established by the supplied material. Basin-scale submerged positioning and storm-stable floating land remain separate innovations.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish whether POSYDON’s scheduled full demonstration occurred, what performance it achieved or whether a basin-scale service was deployed.

The field-wide availability of persistent basin-scale submerged positioning remains undetermined for November 1 or November 11, 2026; the pages are undated and the supplied freshness-search record is empty.
The relative contributions of propagation uncertainty, source geometry, timing, source-position error and receiver motion require technical evidence and a quantitative error budget.
The environmental mechanisms retained from the research lack individual substantiation and quantitative treatment in the supplied reviewed sources.

The feasibility of the proposed several-week, few-tens-of-metres trial with sparse, pre-existing sources has not been established, including how to obtain a sufficiently independent reference trajectory throughout the mission.
Comparative performance and infrastructure dependence of regional acoustic baselines, terrain matching and quantum-inertial approaches remain unassessed by the supplied evidence.
The WHOI overview does not resolve the earlier specific attribution about surfacing for GPS and Iridium; that statement has therefore not been restored.

brief.title: Knowing your location across an ocean while submerged
possible: Underwater vehicles could follow long survey routes and return to mapped work sites without surfacing to learn their position. A few distant sound sources would provide reference points: vehicles would measure their distance from those sources to work out where they are.
The goal is dependable positioning across an ocean basin during missions lasting weeks to months, without installing a network of sound transmitters around each work area.
why: GPS satellite signals cannot penetrate seawater. Dependable underwater positioning would remove a major constraint on long missions and give multiple vehicles a shared geographic reference.
Survey teams could repeat routes and revisit work sites more reliably. Better positioning would also support coordinated fleets and sustained operations without a nearby support vessel.

sources.showed: DARPA outlined a system that would locate submerged vehicles using distant sound sources across ocean basins. Its POSYDON program is complete, but the summary gives no achieved positioning accuracy.
sources.cited_for: The goal of continuous positioning across ocean basins without surfacing for satellite fixes.
sources.not_established: Sustained, accurate positioning for a moving submerged vehicle across an ocean basin has not been established.

sources.showed: WHOI describes Slocum underwater gliders that stay at sea for weeks to months and carry satellite positioning and communication equipment.
sources.quote: They are equipped with oceanographic sensors, a global positioning system (GPS) receiver, and an Iridium satellite modem that allows two-way communication with a shore-side computer.
sources.cited_for: Existing underwater vehicles can undertake long missions and carry satellite navigation equipment.
sources.not_established: Long endurance does not establish continuous positioning while submerged across an ocean basin.

shown: DARPA’s completed POSYDON program targeted positioning across ocean basins, with work planned on sound propagation, signal design and a complete system demonstration. Its achieved accuracy and sustained performance remain unclear.

WHOI describes underwater gliders with weeks-to-months endurance. That establishes the long mission context, while dependable positioning throughout such submerged journeys remains to be demonstrated.
missing: A moving vehicle needs to demonstrate sustained, accurate positioning across a basin using sparse, distant sound sources.
Independent measurements throughout a mission need to establish position errors, service interruptions and the reliability of uncertainty estimates.
Repeated trials need to establish performance across different routes, depths and ocean conditions.
The service needs a measured operating range and clear requirements for transmitters, receivers, maintenance and outside support.

milestones.label: Weeks of accurate positioning across a basin
milestones.explanation: A submerged vehicle would have to cross a basin for weeks using sparse, pre-existing distant sound sources, with errors within a few tens of metres. This would establish sustained positioning without a local array.

milestones.label: Independent comparisons establish errors and service availability
milestones.explanation: An independent reference would have to measure errors throughout the mission, accounting for reference uncertainty and shared errors under predefined update and outage rules. This would establish how consistently positioning works.

milestones.label: Repeated trials establish performance across ocean conditions
milestones.explanation: Trials would have to span different routes, depths and conditions, with enough detail for independent assessment and replication where feasible. This would establish breadth; claims of months of operation would need matching trials.

milestones.label: Operating limits and equipment requirements are established
milestones.explanation: Results would have to define coverage, depths, source spacing, maintenance, receiver size and power, and outside support needs. These boundaries would establish where sustained mobile positioning delivers measured accuracy and availability.

uncertain: Can sparse, distant sound sources support the proposed accuracy throughout a weeks-long basin crossing?
How much error comes from sound propagation, timing, source locations, source arrangement and vehicle motion?
Can an independent reference track the vehicle accurately enough throughout the mission to judge performance?

page.title: Basin-scale acoustic positioning
page.definition: A permanent network of distant underwater sound sources lets moving submerged vehicles determine their geographic positions across an ocean basin. Receivers infer distances from acoustic travel times and obtain position updates without surfacing for satellite navigation.

goal.need: WHOI describes Slocum gliders that travel at less than 1 knot and remain at sea for weeks to months. GPS signals cannot penetrate seawater. Providing geographic fixes underwater would let such vehicles update their positions throughout submerged missions without returning to the surface for satellite navigation.

statements.quote: continuous, accurate positioning without surfacing for a GPS fix
statements.context: POSYDON’s programme summary describes positioning across ocean basins using ranges to a small number of distant acoustic sources.

statements.body: National Research Council, Committee on an Ocean Infrastructure Strategy for U.S. Ocean Research in 2030
statements.quote: Permanent, large-scale subsurface acoustic positional networks (analogous to GPS) for improved undersea navigation
statements.context: Table 4.1 lists this under capabilities to be developed for submersible platforms and autonomous systems.

completion.title: A commissioned acoustic network provides basin-scale position updates to submerged vehicles.
completion.criterion: A network of distant acoustic sources is commissioned for continuing service and demonstrates geographic position updates on moving submerged vehicles across an ocean basin without surfacing for GPS. The public sources provide no numerical acceptance limits for service accuracy, availability, update interval or duration.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback combining the NRC permanent-network goal with DARPA’s POSYDON positioning objective.
completion.basis: Searched DARPA’s POSYDON summary, DARPA-BAA-15-30 sections 1.2–1.4 and NRC Table 4.1. These give a permanent-network goal and prototype demonstration tests, but no public acceptance test for a continuing basin-scale service. DARPA’s numerical programme-success metrics are classified. This fallback retains permanent infrastructure and submerged position updates without adding numerical cutoffs.

milestones.title: At-sea measurements validate acoustic models across deep-ocean and continental-shelf environments.
milestones.criterion: Validate acoustic measurement models and source waveforms against at-sea data in deep ocean, continental shelves and shipping channels; Phase I permits offline processing. Partial evidence: a 2023 reanalysis of 502 moored-hydrophone positions from the Philippine Sea experiment in 2010 and 2011, with six sources 129–450 km away, reduced mean position error from 58 m to 25 m using ocean-model corrections. It required 40 manual offset corrections affecting 30 positions.
milestones.set_by: DARPA, DARPA-BAA-15-30, sections 1.2 and 1.3.1.3: POSYDON Phase I validation.
milestones.threshold_quote: validate the measurement models and assess signal availability

milestones.title: An acoustic receiver measures source ranges in real time.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate acoustic source-to-receiver ranging in real time, the POSYDON Phase II test. Regional evidence: Beaufort Sea experiments from 8 March 2020 to 11 March 2020 reported mean absolute beacon-to-beacon range errors of 11.38 m for 243 events and 11.36 m for 568 events, using two sound-speed profiles, at distances up to approximately 3 km. Those tests used surface-supported processing; they do not establish basin-scale ranging.
milestones.set_by: DARPA, DARPA-BAA-15-30, section 1.2: POSYDON Phase II demonstration.

milestones.title: An integrated acoustic positioning system passes a government-validated real-time demonstration.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate an integrated POSYDON positioning system in real time, with government validation of all components. Partial mobile evidence: a 2022 offline analysis of 2,111 receptions from four Philippine Sea gliders, recorded from November 2010 to April 2011 at ranges up to 700 km and depths down to 1,000 m, yielded 55 m root-mean-square positioning residuals with a 150 m fault-detection threshold. These measure range consistency. The gliders surfaced between dives. No public government-validation result was located.
milestones.set_by: DARPA, DARPA-BAA-15-30, section 1.2: POSYDON Phase III integrated demonstration; numerical success metrics are in the classified addendum.
milestones.threshold_quote: an integrated system demonstration and validation of all POSYDON components

not_found: No public numerical POSYDON success metrics were found; DARPA places them in a classified addendum.
No public report establishing the outcome of POSYDON’s government-validated integrated demonstration or commissioning of a permanent basin-scale service was located.
No separate laboratory acceptance test was found in the public POSYDON documents.

results.finding: A digital acoustic waveform achieved symbol error rates of 4.8% or less for the first six symbols across 42 transmissions.
results.detail: The waveform was demonstrated over a 3,500 km acoustic path, but the text does not establish validation across deep-ocean, continental-shelf and shipping-channel environments. Later-symbol performance degraded.
results.quote: Analysis of 42 transmissions at a 75-Hz center frequency shows symbol error rates of 4.8% or less for the first six symbols, with later-symbol performance degrading, consistent with finite channel coherence.
